docs/plans/2026-04-06-memo-mentions/design.md:25:Research also suggests that Memos should stay narrower than Notion or Confluence. There is no existing concept of teams, group mentions, page mentions, or per-page ACLs. The codebase already treats usernames as the public user token and memo visibility as a coarse `PUBLIC/PROTECTED/PRIVATE` rule. The best fit is therefore person mentions only, keyed by canonical username, with notification rules that are access-aware and deduplicated across repeated edits.
docs/plans/2026-04-06-memo-mentions/design.md:43:- Redesigning memo visibility or introducing user-level memo sharing.
docs/plans/2026-04-06-memo-mentions/design.md:57:Apply access and duplication rules before writing inbox rows. Self-mentions are ignored. For top-level memos, notify only when the target can already read the memo under current visibility rules. For comments, notify the mentioned user when they can read the comment context and are not already covered by the existing memo-comment notification to the parent memo owner for that same event. This keeps mention notifications meaningful and avoids sending an owner both a comment notification and a mention notification for the same comment creation unless future product requirements explicitly want both. For `PRIVATE` memos and `PRIVATE` comments, mentions remain author-visible text but do not generate inbox notifications for other users.

docs/plans/2026-04-06-memo-mentions/design.md:25:Research also suggests that Memos should stay narrower than Notion or Confluence. There is no existing concept of teams, group mentions, page mentions, or per-page ACLs. The codebase already treats usernames as the public user token and memo visibility as a coarse `PUBLIC/PROTECTED/PRIVATE` rule. The best fit is therefore person mentions only, keyed by canonical username, with notification rules that are access-aware and deduplicated across repeated edits.
docs/plans/2026-04-06-memo-mentions/design.md:43:- Redesigning memo visibility or introducing user-level memo sharing.
docs/plans/2026-04-06-memo-mentions/design.md:57:Apply access and duplication rules before writing inbox rows. Self-mentions are ignored. For top-level memos, notify only when the target can already read the memo under current visibility rules. For comments, notify the mentioned user when they can read the comment context and are not already covered by the existing memo-comment notification to the parent memo owner for that same event. This keeps mention notifications meaningful and avoids sending an owner both a comment notification and a mention notification for the same comment creation unless future product requirements explicitly want both. For `PRIVATE` memos and `PRIVATE` comments, mentions remain author-visible text but do not generate inbox notifications for other users.

I'm noting that FindMemo's visibility list is translated into SQL filters in the store layer, which is the shared enforcement mechanism rather than a separate check point, and the CEL filter engine also handles visibility filtering. I want to check the fileserver for share-token routes like a public "s/{token}" page and confirm whether GetMemoByShare intentionally bypasses visibility checks, plus look at the connect interceptor.

I should also check for an allowlist of unauthenticated methods, and verify where checkMemoReadAccess is actually called from, including whether handlers like ListMemoRelations or GetMemoActivity use it.

Now I have enough to write the answer, organizing enforcement sites by server surface—starting with the Connect/gRPC memo read path, then the list path with its viewer-scoped store filters.

Beyond that, comment surfaces, reaction service, attachment metadata and raw file serving each have their own access checks, along with RSS feeds and the sitemap being public-only, SSE fan-out checks, user stats endpoints, and the share-token surface—each with its own file and line references marking where enforcement happens.

I'm also noting the notification and mention gating logic, which seems more about redacting content in inbox listings than viewing permissions itself, but I want to verify how user_service_notifications.go and email.go handle memo content before deciding whether it belongs in the same category. There's also a shared enforcement mechanism at the store layer across the different database backends that applies visibility filters, which I should check next alongside the notification code.

I'm finding two more places with duplicated access-check logic: notification listing that redacts memo content, and email dispatch, plus the mention-notification gating in memo_mention_helpers.go. I want to trace how canViewerAccessMemo is used in user_service_notifications.go, then double-check the SSE streaming endpoint before I finalize my understanding.

Now I'll organize the full list of enforcement sites — primary memo-viewing checks and secondary ones — with file paths and line references, verifying the store layer's visibility SQL to cite accurately.

Now I'll format the answer as a list of enforcement sites with their paths, one per line, plus a brief note that they share a common store mechanism even though the checks themselves are duplicated rather than centralized.

h15.

Memo visibility is not centralized in one authorizer — each surface that can expose memo data re-implements the same PUBLIC / PROTECTED / PRIVATE rule. Here are the distinct enforcement sites:

Single-memo read check (`checkMemoReadAccess`, used by `GetMemo` and `ListMemoComments`) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` (lines 39–68, called at 356/367 and from `memo_service_comments.go:148`)
Memo list query scoping (`ListMemos` builds a viewer-scoped `VisibilityList` / CEL filter) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` (lines 218–227)
Comment creation and comment list scoping (`CreateMemoComment` private check; `ListMemoComments` per-viewer `memoFilter`) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go` (lines 41–43, 156–161)
Reaction service (`ListMemoReactions`, `UpsertMemoReaction`, `DeleteMemoReaction`) — `server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go` (lines 29–41, 82–85, 130–140)
Memo attachment listing (`ListMemoAttachments`) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go` (lines 213–225)
Attachment metadata access via API (`checkAttachmentAccess`, used by `GetAttachment`) — `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go` (lines 419–455)
Raw blob/thumbnail serving over HTTP (`checkAttachmentPermission`, includes the anonymous-instance and `share_token` branches) — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 650–704)
SSE event fan-out filter (`SSEClient.canReceive`) — `server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go` (lines 134–144)
User stats aggregation (`ListAllUserStats`, `GetUserStats`) — `server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go` (lines 83–92, 217–221)
Notification payload redaction (`canViewerAccessMemo` gating inbox notification content) — `server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go` (lines 302–316, used at 337/342/370/385)
Email notification dispatch (its own duplicate `canViewerAccessMemo`) — `server/notification/email.go` (lines 306–320, used at 155/187)
Mention-notification eligibility (private memos/comments don't notify others) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go` (lines 62–84)
Public feed surfaces, which hard-code `VisibilityList: {Public}` — `server/router/rss/rss.go` (lines 90, 141) and `server/router/frontend/frontend.go` (sitemap, line 150)
Share-token bypass path (`GetMemoByShare` returns a memo of any visibility once the token is valid and unexpired; token creation restricted to creator/admin) — `server/router/api/v1/memo_share_service.go` (lines 23–45, 151–208)

The query-scoping sites all funnel into the same store mechanism, which translates `FindMemo.VisibilityList` into a SQL `IN` clause per driver: `store/memo.go:69`, `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:96`, `store/db/postgres/memo.go:89`, `store/db/mysql/memo.go:104`. That is the shared mechanism, not an independent decision point — the decision of which visibilities to allow is made in each caller listed above.
